//: Example gofin configuration. Copy it and edit:
cp gofin.example.json gofin.json
./gofin serve --dry-run      # prints the resolved config, starts nothing
./gofin serve
gofin looks for ./gofin.json by default; -config or GOFIN_CONFIG picks
another path. Precedence is defaults, then this file, then GOFIN_* env vars,
then command-line flags -- each layer overriding the one before it. Only
flags you actually type override the file, so a flag left at its default
will not quietly replace a value set here.
Every key below may be deleted; the built-in default then applies. Run
'./gofin config' to print the defaults with no commentary.
Keys named "//" are comments. JSON has none, and gofin ignores unknown
keys, so this is the usual workaround rather than anything gofin-specific.
name           what clients display, and part of the server ID derivation,
so renaming the server changes its ID -- pick one and keep it.
bind           0.0.0.0 for every interface, 127.0.0.1 to accept only local
connections (use this when a reverse proxy sits in front).
port           8096 is the Jellyfin default and what clients probe first.
base_url       set only when served under a sub-path, e.g. "/jellyfin".
A leading slash is added and a trailing one removed for you.
published_url  the externally reachable URL, when it differs from what the
server sees. Clients are handed this for their own links.
Leave empty to derive it from the request.
server.name: Gofin

//: Server state, NOT media -- media lives in "libraries" below.
Relative paths resolve against the working directory; prefer absolute
paths when running under systemd, where that is not what you expect.
These directories are created at startup if missing.
The JELLYFIN_DATA_DIR / JELLYFIN_CONFIG_DIR / JELLYFIN_CACHE_DIR /
JELLYFIN_LOG_DIR env vars also set these, so gofin drops into an
existing Jellyfin container without rewriting its environment.
Media roots. Each becomes one library in the client.
name      what clients display. Defaults to the directory name.
Must be unique, compared case-insensitively.
path      absolute path to the media root. Required. It must exist and
be readable at startup or gofin exits rather than starting up
and presenting an empty library.
type      movies, tvshows, music, musicvideos, homevideos, boxsets,
books, or mixed. Omit or use "" for mixed content.
readonly  true keeps gofin from ever writing to the media root.
readonly DEFAULTS TO TRUE when omitted. That is deliberate: the unsafe
value should never be the one you get by saying nothing. Set it to
false only when you want gofin writing into your media directories.
Nothing in this build writes to media at all, so today readonly is a
statement of intent that becomes load-bearing once deletion and
metadata writeback exist. For a hard guarantee, mount the media
read-only as well -- a bind,ro mount is enforced by the kernel, which
no amount of application config can match.
Libraries may not overlap: one root may not contain another, since
every file in the overlap would resolve twice under two different
parents and two different item IDs.
libraries.name: Movies

//: Artwork and metadata providers. OFF by default: a media server should
not start reaching the internet because a config file gained a field.
TMDB (themoviedb.org) supplies movie posters. To turn it on you need
your OWN free API key:
1. sign up at https://www.themoviedb.org/signup
2. request an API key at https://www.themoviedb.org/settings/api
3. paste it into api_key below, set enabled to true, restart
USE YOUR OWN KEY. Jellyfin ships a hardcoded one in its source and it is
deliberately not reused here: that key belongs to the Jellyfin project,
TMDB's terms require an application to use its own, and borrowing it
would risk getting THEIR key rate-limited by our traffic.
The key is a credential. If you would rather not have it sit in a file
that gets copied around, leave api_key empty and set the environment
variable GOFIN_TMDB_API_KEY instead -- that also enables the provider.
poster_size is a TMDB size bucket: w92, w154, w185, w342, w500, w780,
or original. w500 is the default here. Jellyfin defaults to original,
which for a large library means downloading many megabytes per film to
render a thumbnail a few hundred pixels wide.
language is an ISO code like en-US, es-MX, ja-JP. It selects which
localised poster is preferred.
Posters are written to <cache>/images/, NEVER next to your media -- a
readonly library stays untouched. Deleting that directory costs only
bandwidth. Titles TMDB cannot match get a .miss marker so they are not
looked up again on every restart; POST /Library/RefreshArtwork with
?retryMissed=true clears those after you rename the offending files.
password is a bootstrap convenience: it is hashed with PBKDF2-SHA512
when the config loads. It is NOT hashed in this file, so a config with
a plaintext password in it should be mode 0600 and should not be
committed anywhere.
To avoid storing plaintext at all, put an already-hashed value in
password_hash instead and drop the password field. The format is
$PBKDF2-SHA512$iterations=N$<salt-hex>$<digest-hex>, and the iteration
count is read from the string rather than assumed -- so hashes exported
from an existing Jellyfin user table verify as they are.
User IDs are derived from the name, so a user keeps the same ID across
restarts and across machines. Renaming a user changes their ID.
CHANGE THIS PASSWORD before exposing the server to anything.
users.name: admin

//: Serve a jellyfin-web dist from disk. Leave disabled for an API-only
server; point dir at an unpacked jellyfin-web build to serve the UI too.
level   trace, debug, info, warn, or error. debug logs every request.
format  text for humans, json for a log collector.
Every unimplemented endpoint logs itself at WARN, so browsing with a real
client at debug level produces a prioritized list of what to build next.
